newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentines without receipts could face big fines.
newsitem.headline: Argentines without receipts could face big fines.

text.p: Argentines who do not demand receipts for goods or services could face fines of up to $1,670 under a plan presented by Argentina's top taxman.
Carlos Silvani, head of the DGI tax department presented his planned bill to members of the Budget and Finance Committee of the Chamber of Deputies late Thursday.

Fines would run from $167 to $1,670 for consumers nabbed without receipts by tax inspectors under the scheme, which is aimed to make buyers demand that shopkeepers keep a legal record of all transactions.

Oscar Lamberto, president of the Budget and Finance Committee and a member of the governing Peronist Party, was cautiously in favor of the idea, telling the El Cronista newspaper: "It's not a matter of snooping on consumers, but of persuading society that giving receipts and paying taxes is part of a civilized community."
But the daily La Nacion quoted other Peronist deputies saying they would vote against the project.

Argentina's government has launched a series of campaigns to crack down on endemic tax evasion in recent years. According to the Clarin newspaper Friday, the DGI is involved in a total of 700,000 court actions over alleged tax-dodging.
